A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MFPG research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including material reorganized between versions.

before.justification: V3 reports original MuJoCo experiments, policy-gradient variance measurements, reward-misspecification experiments, and ablations in Section 6 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V4 reports original benchmark and ablation results in Section 6 and Appendices D–E, including expanded evaluations using 20 random seeds.

M1.justification: The MFPG–REINFORCE procedure retains its control variate, shared-noise trajectory sampling, moving-average coefficient estimation, shared value baseline, and negative-correlation safeguard. Expanded iteration notation and Algorithm 2 clarify the existing procedure without establishing a changed implementation.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same 39 Hopper, Walker2d, and HalfCheetah dynamics settings and the negated-reward experiment. V4 separates 15 main settings from 24 appendix settings; kinematic variations remain covered in Appendix E.

E2.justification: High-Fidelity Only, Low-Fidelity Only (100×), DARC, PAR, and More High-Fidelity Data (15×) remain evaluated. The 15× reference is retained for corresponding tasks in v4 Figures 14 and 16, despite its omission from the main difference plots.

E3.justification: Section 6.1 revises the reported aggregation from median/minimum/maximum return curves to per-run metrics summarized by means; primary comparisons use mean differences from High-Fidelity Only. Training budgets, evaluation cadence, evaluation episodes, and Table 1 hyperparameters are retained.

E4.justification: The sample-budget, moving-average, reparameterization, and trajectory-reconstraining studies retain their questions but receive revised empirical evidence and findings. For example, the batch-size analysis now identifies a small significant benefit at 2000 samples. Moving the existing reparameterization and reconstraining studies to Appendix D is not a new ablation.

E5.justification: V3 generally reports five-seed medians and extrema. V4 uses 20 seeds for Sections 6.3–6.5, adds two-sided 95% bootstrap intervals using 10,000 resamples, and tests mean differences against High-Fidelity Only. Appendix boxplots add distribution summaries; the variance study and 24 additional settings retain five-seed reporting.

E6.justification: Main benchmark and ablation summaries are extensively replaced by 20-seed estimates and significance findings. Figure 3 supports significant MFPG gains in all eight mild-to-moderate Hopper-gravity and Walker2d-friction settings, while Figure 7 revises v3's no-further-benefit finding at batch size 2000. These are revised estimates under different seed counts and aggregation, not direct performance improvements over v3.

T1.justification: V4 adds Lemma 1 and an Appendix B proof of control-variate unbiasedness and variance reduction, previously stated without that proof. Section 3 also corrects the reward-to-go expression from summing gamma^t r_t to summing gamma^(n-t) r_n. The convergence theorem and its existing proof are substantively retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion refine the empirical claim from matching leading methods in median performance to consistent significant mean improvements when low-fidelity data are neutral or beneficial. They explicitly acknowledge that competing methods can achieve higher returns. The central methodological and convergence contributions remain.

C2.justification: V4 develops the interpretation that MFPG trades aggressive exploitation of low-fidelity data for reliability. Section 7 and new Appendix G substantially expand applicability limits, explaining biased actor-critic estimators, difficulties with TD-based and offline methods, and requirements for reconstructing correlated trajectories. Five-seed appendix results are explicitly restricted to qualitative conclusions.

D1.justification: V4 clarifies fidelity-specific Monte Carlo returns, shared value-function subtraction, and iteration-level implementation details. Access information changes from v3's direct repository release statement to project-site and supplementary-material pointers alongside future-release wording. Table 1 configurations remain unchanged; actual online availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: V4 adds references and discussion concerning deficient-support off-dynamics RL, newer offline adaptation methods, and actor-critic/offline bias and variance issues. The main positioning against Khairy and Balaprakash, DARC, and PAR remains intact.

P1.justification: Sections 3–4 substantially expand the estimator and sampling explanations, and Section 6 extensively rewrites the experimental narrative around statistical comparisons. The conclusion gains a structured limitations discussion, and appendices are reorganized to separate proofs, ablations, additional results, implementation details, and extensions.

P2.justification: Main result plots are redesigned around baseline-relative mean differences and confidence intervals. Appendix E adds complementary difference plots and boxplots, splits the former combined benchmark displays, and retains the high-fidelity reference comparisons. Captions, legends, algorithm blocks, and document typography also change substantially.

improvement.justification: V3's central reliability claims rested on noisy five-seed medians and extrema. V4 substantially strengthens their evidential basis through 20-seed evaluations and bootstrap comparisons in Figures 3–9, while distinguishing significant gains, neutral effects, and failures. Explicitly limiting the remaining five-seed evidence and expanding applicability limitations improve the calibration of its conclusions. Less clear code-release wording is a limited drawback relative to these gains.
